theater: 愛琴海與赫勒斯滂海峽

battle.name: 同盟者戰爭
battle.theater: 愛琴海與赫勒斯滂海峽
battle.brief: 公元前357至前355年，雅典第二帝國與聯盟島邦希俄斯、羅得、科斯及拜占庭在愛琴海與安那托利亞沿岸開戰。島邦指控雅典挪用同盟稅金、獨佔黑海糧道，聯軍遂封鎖赫勒斯滂海峽；雅典先後派出卡雷斯率領數百艘三列槳船遠征，提謨修斯的分隊最終在拜占庭外海覆滅。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰一方是雅典第二帝國，也就是以雅典城邦為核心的第二雅典同盟：雅典出重裝步兵、輕裝矛兵與海軍，同盟成員按比例繳納同盟稅並供應船隻，稅金存放在雅典城內的共同庫房，由公民議會支配。公元前357年時，第二同盟仍握有愛琴海東岸與赫勒斯滂海峽一帶的關鍵島嶼與據點，實力核心是雅典的三列槳艦隊與城牆重兵。另一方是島邦聯軍：希俄斯、羅得、科斯三座島嶼的艦隊與登陸兵，加上脫離雅典管治的拜占庭城邦；這些城邦多年來承擔遠洋巡航與海峽警戒，擁有自有的造船能力與經驗老到的水手。第三方是斯巴達：國王阿基達穆斯三世以同盟的名義把三座島嶼接納進赫倫尼克聯盟，並派兵佔領色雷斯的刻爾索涅斯地峽，切斷雅典在北方的殖民地。波斯國王阿爾達薛西斯三世默許甚至鼓勵島邦脫離雅典，並承諾一旦開戰便從小亞細亞出兵；這層背書是島邦敢於公開叛離的關鍵底氣。埃及的托勒密二世保持中立，卻照舊以穀物船與雅典往來。指揮系統上，雅典每次出動都由十人將軍委員會輪流領兵，本次投入卡雷斯、卡布里亞斯、提謨修斯、伊菲克拉特斯等人；島邦聯軍沒有統一指揮，各城邦自行決定出兵規模；斯巴達則以國王與少數將領為核心，戰事在海峽、刻爾索涅斯與色雷斯多線同時進行，雅典很難用一次勝利扭轉全局。
countriesEn: The war pitted the Second Athenian Empire, that is the Second Athenian League centred on the city of Athens, against a coalition of allied poleis. Athens provided hoplites, peltasts and a fleet, while league members paid the phoros tribute in cash and in ships; the common treasury was kept in Athens and remained under the control of the citizen assembly. By 357 BC the league still held the decisive islands and anchorages of the eastern Aegean and of the Hellespont, and the real weight of its power lay in the Athenian trireme fleet and the garrisoned city. On the other side stood the island coalition: the fleets and landing parties of Chios, Rhodes and Cos, joined by the city of Byzantium which had thrown off Athenian control. These states had for years carried the burden of long-range cruising and of policing the straits, and they possessed their own shipbuilding capacity and crews of long experience. A third party was Sparta: King Archidamus III received the three islands into the Hellenic League and sent troops to occupy the Thracian Chersonese, cutting off the northern cleruchies of Athens. The Persian king Artaxerxes III tacitly approved, indeed encouraged, the revolt and promised to intervene from Asia Minor once war began; that endorsement was the decisive reassurance for the rebels. Ptolemy II of Egypt remained neutral but continued to send grain ships to Athens. On the Athenian side command was organised through the board of ten generals, and this war brought in Chares, Chabrias, Timotheus and Iphicrates. The island coalition had no unified command and each polis decided its own contingent. The Spartan effort centred on the king and a handful of commanders, with fighting going on at the same time in the straits, the Chersonese and Thrace, so that no single Athenian victory could turn the war.
people: 關鍵人物集中在雅典將軍與斯巴達國王兩端。卡雷斯是這場戰爭中聲量最大的雅典將軍，以口才與煽動群眾的能力著稱；出征時他攜帶大量水手、平民與乘客同行，甚至在甲板上召開全體市民大會，讓船上的每個人都能聽他陳述戰況與訴求。這既顯示他的個人威望，也暴露遠征軍隊編制鬆散、水手經驗參差的實況。卡布里亞斯是年齡最長、經驗最深的雅典將軍，作風穩健，他主要對付斯巴達方面，在埃姆巴塔海戰中以守為攻的船隊戰術重創斯巴達艦隊。伊菲克拉特斯以裝備改革聞名，他改造矛、盾、鎧的規格並提高輕裝兵軍餉，其部隊在色雷斯戰線上屢建戰功。提謨修斯是整場戰爭最令人扼腕的人物：他出身雅典名門，父祖兩代都為城邦立過大功，公元前356年率六十餘艘三列槳船開赴赫勒斯滂海峽企圖解拜占庭之圍，卻在島邦聯軍的攻擊下損失慘重，僅以少數船隻逃回；雅典人隨即以叛國罪在陪審法庭審他，由一千五百名公民組成的大陪審團判其無罪，他仍舊鬱鬱而終，此後名字與敗績綁在一起。島邦一方的領袖姓名在古典記載中大多無名，只能確定三座島嶼各自派出執政官與艦隊指揮。卡里亞的毛羅斯與波斯使者往返穿梭於島邦之間遊說它們脫離雅典；斯巴達王阿基達穆斯三世在戰局僵持時提供庇護與接納；色雷斯王克列索布勒普特斯則趁雅典分身乏術，收回先前割讓的色雷斯土地。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities sit at the two ends of the conflict: the Athenian generals and the Spartan king. Chares was the loudest Athenian commander of the war, famous for his eloquence and his ability to stir a crowd; on campaign he carried large numbers of sailors, civilians and passengers with him and even held a general assembly of the citizens aboard ship, so that every man on board could hear his account of the war and his demands. That showed his personal authority and at the same time exposed how loosely the expedition was organised and how uneven the seamanship of the crews was. Chabrias, the oldest and most experienced of the Athenian generals, was a cautious man; he concentrated on the Spartan front and at the naval battle of Embata used a defensive fleet technique that wrecked the Spartan squadron. Iphicrates was known for reforming equipment: he altered the length of the spear, the size of the shield and the pattern of the body armour, and he raised the pay of the peltasts; his troops scored repeated successes on the Thracian front. Timotheus is the most tragic figure of the whole war. He came from a distinguished Athenian family whose forebears had twice served the state with distinction; in 356 BC he sailed for the Hellespont with more than sixty triremes to relieve Byzantium, suffered a disastrous defeat at the hands of the island coalition and returned with only a handful of ships. The Athenians then put him on trial for treason before the law courts, where a jury of fifteen hundred citizens acquitted him; he nevertheless died of grief, and his name was thereafter bound to the failure. The leaders of the island states are for the most part nameless in the ancient sources; we can only establish that each of the three islands sent its own magistrates and ship commanders. Mausolus of Caria and Persian emissaries travelled among the islands urging them to leave Athens; King Archidamus III gave them protection and admission once the fighting stalled; and the Thracian king Cersobleptes took advantage of Athens' distraction to recover Thracian land previously ceded.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及月牙劍，一把外彎的青銅單刃短劍：刃口內凹、背脊加厚、劍尖向前彎成鉤狀，揮砍時把全身重量壓上去，不必把劍拔出來；它興於古埃及中王國，至新王國早期仍見於軍中，約在公元前12世紀之後退出戰場，是比希臘世界早出數百年的老兵器。必須說清它在這場戰爭中的位置：公元前357年的愛琴海沒有一支部隊使用月牙劍。島邦聯軍與雅典實際上手持的是希臘式雙刃短劍，以及色雷斯式彎刃單刃刀——後者砍下去不用拔的使用邏輯，與月牙劍同出一源，可視為同一兵器思想在色雷斯的延伸。步兵配置上，重裝方陣兵用圓盾、長矛與青銅頭盔，縱隊與方陣交替；輕裝的佩爾塔斯特用新月盾與短矛，正是伊菲克拉特斯改造矛盾的對象。海上，三列槳與四列槳戰船是主力，銅質船喙負責撞擊，另有抓鈎、登舷用的攻城梯與纏鬥用的接舷纜；遠征軍隊還需貨船運載步兵、攻城器與數週份的糧秣淡水。所以月牙劍在這場戰爭裡的位置，是技術譜系與象徵層面的：一頭連著古埃及的青銅工藝與單刃砍劈傳統，另一頭連著色雷斯的彎刃刀；它同時提醒人注意一條容易被忽略的貿易線——托勒密二世治下的埃及雖然不是交戰方，卻以穀物船與雅典維持生意，而塞浦路斯的王權與波斯使者的腳步也都捲入地中海東部的整體角力。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian khopesh, a curved bronze single-edged short sword: the edge is concave, the spine is thickened and the point curves forward into a hook, so that the wielder puts his whole weight into the blow and never has to wrench the blade back out of the target. It arose in the Middle Kingdom of Egypt and was still seen in the army of the early New Kingdom, falling out of service around the twelfth century BC, several centuries before the Greek world it would later be compared with. Its place in this war must be stated plainly: in 357 BC no army in the Aegean carried a khopesh. The island coalition and the Athenians actually wielded the straight double-edged Greek short sword and the Thracian curved single-edged blade, the naue, whose cut-and-without-pulling logic is of a piece with the khopesh and can be read as the same idea carried into Thrace. On foot, the armoured hoplite carried the round shield, the long spear and a bronze helmet, alternating column and phalanx; the light peltast with his crescent-shaped shield and short spear was exactly the man whose equipment Iphicrates rewrote. At sea the trireme and the quadrireme were the workhorses, with bronze rams for breaking the enemy, plus grappling irons, boarding ladders and cables for tying ships together; the expedition also needed merchant hulls to move infantry, siege gear and several weeks of rations and fresh water. The khopesh therefore stands in this war at the level of technical lineage and symbol: at one end the bronze craft and the single-edged chopping tradition of Egypt, at the other the curved blades of Thrace. It also points at an easily overlooked commercial thread, for Egypt under Ptolemy II, though not a belligerent, kept trading grain ships with Athens, and the kingship of Cyprus and the footsteps of the Persian emissaries were likewise drawn into the wider struggle of the eastern Mediterranean.
tactics: 島邦聯軍的戰術核心是控扼海峽。拜占庭扼守黑海小麥航線的咽喉，聯軍佔下這座城，就等於掐住雅典的糧食與稅源；希俄斯、羅得、科斯的水手熟悉赫勒斯滂海峽的潮流與暗礁，狹窄水道中大船難以迴轉，島邦多用途的快船佔盡便宜。聯軍多採騷擾與掠奪式的打法：攔截往來商船、切斷雅典的外島據點、登陸奇襲港口，再用小船散開，使雅典無法集中兵力逐個殲滅。雅典這一邊的戰術問題是分兵與經驗。遠征艦隊雖大，卻分成卡雷斯、提謨修斯、伊菲克拉特斯等數支，互不協同；水手多為臨時徵召的市民，操船技術參差，一旦進入狹窄海峽便難以佈陣。提謨修斯率小隊企圖封鎖海峽、解救拜占庭，選擇了最不利的地形；島邦聯軍則集中快船突擊其側翼，雅典艦隊在潮流與亂陣中崩潰，損失大半。與此同時，雅典在另一條戰線上以卡布里亞斯的守勢船術應對斯巴達：埃姆巴塔海戰中水手躲在艙板下，拒絕讓敵方船喙發揮衝撞力，改以船首纏鬥、接舷肉搏取勝；伊菲克拉特斯則在色雷斯與當地王克列索布勒普特斯聯手，擋住斯巴達軍隊渡海。政治戰線上，島邦聯軍把爭議提交安菲克提翁會議仲裁，雅典拒絕受理，並以公民大會作為後盾，把遠征的理由直接訴諸民眾；提謨修斯的案子則交由陪審法庭裁決，說明雅典的將領連在海外也要受城邦司法管束。補給方面，遠征船隊須隨船攜帶數週糧秣與淡水，冬季海峽風浪大，補給線拉得極長，一旦被游騎封鎖就難以為繼。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of the island coalition was the control of the straits. Byzantium commanded the throat of the Black Sea grain route, so by taking that city the coalition put a hand on the throat of Athenian food and revenue alike. The pilots of Chios, Rhodes and Cos knew the currents and shoals of the Hellespont, large ships could hardly turn in the narrow water, and the coalition's handy galleys had the advantage on every count. Its method was harassment and plunder: intercepting merchantmen, cutting Athenian island outposts, raiding harbours by surprise landings, and then scattering in small squadrons so that Athens could never concentrate force to destroy them one at a time. The Athenian tactical problem was dispersal and inexperience. The expedition fleet was large but split into squadrons under Chares, Timotheus, Iphicrates and others, none of them working in concert; the crews were largely citizens mustered at short notice, their seamanship uneven, and once in the narrow straits they could hardly be dressed into line. Timotheus took a small force into the straits to relieve Byzantium and block the passage, choosing the worst possible ground, and the coalition concentrated its fast ships against his flank; the Athenian fleet broke up in the current and the confusion and lost the greater part of its strength. On the other front Athens met the Spartans with Chabrias' defensive seamanship: at Embata the crews kept under the deck boards, denying the enemy rams their effect, and the victory was won by holding ships together prow to prow and fighting hand to hand after boarding. Iphicrates, meanwhile, joined the Thracian king Cersobleptes and blocked a Spartan crossing. On the political front the coalition appealed its dispute to the Amphictyonic arbitration, which Athens refused to accept, and Athens answered with the general assembly of the citizens, putting the case for the expedition directly to the populace; the case of Timotheus went to a jury court, which shows that even abroad an Athenian general remained answerable to the justice of his own polis. On the logistic side, expedition fleets had to carry several weeks of rations and fresh water with them, the winter gales in the straits were severe, the supply line was stretched to breaking point, and once the squadrons were blockaded it could not be sustained.
data: 可核對的數字並不多，且多出自古史家狄奧多羅斯。其一，公元前357年雅典出動的海軍規模：卡雷斯率領四百艘三列槳船，提謨修斯六十艘，伊菲克拉特斯等將軍各率數十艘，總數逾六百艘；後世另有卡雷斯率八百艘之說，多被視為誇大，因為水手編制、護衛艦比例與糧秣需求都難以支撐這樣的數目。其二，提謨修斯受審時的陪審規模為一千五百名公民。其三，同期埃姆巴塔海戰中斯巴達艦隊折損的船數，各家記載在數十艘之間，未見確數；島邦聯軍的艦隊總數與雙方死傷人數，在古典文獻中基本空白，只能說這是一場以艦隊與航線為主的消耗戰，留下的是帳目空白而不是傷亡數字。其四，時間跨度：戰爭自公元前357年打到公元前355年，約兩年；同期雅典還在色雷斯方向與斯巴達交戰，又把同盟稅投入福基斯方向的第三神聖戰爭，多線作戰的資源分散，正是戰局崩壞的算術原因。其五，地理尺度：羅得到拜占庭的水道約五百至六百公里，島邦聯軍正是靠這條航線的縱深維持補給；雅典要補上這些被切斷的地段，縱使贏得單場海戰也難以轉成戰略優勢。公元前355年，雅典與斯巴達議和，第二雅典同盟解散，島邦加入斯巴達主導的第二赫倫尼克聯盟。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are few, and most of them come from Diodorus. First, the scale of the Athenian naval dispatch in 357 BC: four hundred triremes under Chares, sixty under Timotheus, and several dozen apiece under generals such as Iphicrates, giving a total of more than six hundred ships. Later tradition speaks of eight hundred ships under Chares, a figure generally treated as inflated, since the size of the crews, the ratio of escort vessels and the food requirements can hardly support it. Second, the jury that tried Timotheus numbered fifteen hundred citizens. Third, the Spartan losses at the naval battle of Embata in the same years are given by different authors as a number of ships in the tens, with no agreed figure; the total strength of the island fleet and the casualties on both sides are essentially blank in the ancient literature, so the only safe statement is that this was a war of fleets and sea lanes fought as a war of attrition, leaving an empty ledger rather than a casualty list. Fourth, the time span: the war ran from 357 to 355 BC, roughly two years, while Athens was simultaneously fighting Sparta in Thrace and sinking league money into the Third Sacred War in the direction of Phocis; the arithmetic of forces spread over too many fronts is the arithmetic reason the position collapsed. Fifth, the geographical scale: the water passage from Rhodes to Byzantium runs about five hundred to six hundred kilometres, and it was precisely the depth of that route which kept the coalition supplied; the stretches Athens had lost could not be restored by winning a single sea battle. In 355 BC Athens made peace with Sparta, the Second Athenian League was dissolved, and the islands entered the Spartan-led Second Hellenic League.
cause: 起火點有明顯的經濟與治理背景。島邦是第二同盟裡出力最多的成員：它們常年派船巡航、護航，承擔克里特與安那托利亞沿岸的戰鬥，卻拿不到與風險相稱的回報。公元前357年雅典在島邦推行新的徵稅安排，要它們照既定比例多繳同盟稅並加派船隻；金幣島的稅令以及其他相關法令，把島邦的負擔一次拉高。更關鍵的是錢的去向：雅典把共同庫房裡的稅金拿來支持底比斯與阿爾戈斯的聯盟，去打福基斯方向的第三神聖戰爭，還支付其他盟國的援助款，島邦最在意的共有錢財被挪用因此爆發。制度上的不滿同樣累積：同盟的重要事務由雅典公民議會決定，島邦居民沒有投票權，也沒有軍事指揮權，卻要在雅典指定的戰場作戰。加上卡里亞的毛羅斯與波斯使者的遊說，島邦看見一個算得清的風險比較——留在同盟裡要繼續分擔雅典的戰爭與稅負，投向斯巴達主導的聯盟則可以保住自治。時機同樣重要：雅典正深陷福基斯戰事與北方的刻爾索涅斯問題，兵力分散在多個方向，防守出現空隙；斯巴達又恰好在北方接應，把幾乎所有備戰的難度都推給了雅典一方。
causeEn: The outbreak had clear economic and administrative causes. The island states contributed the most to the Second League: they cruised and escorted year round and fought along the coasts of Crete and Anatolia, yet received a return proportionate neither to the risk nor to the effort. In 357 BC Athens reorganised the tribute arrangements in the islands, requiring them to pay more phoros than the established rate and to furnish additional ships; the decree touching Chios and the related measures raised the burden on the islands in a single stroke. More decisive was the destination of the money: Athens took the common treasury and used it to support the Theban-Argive coalition against Phocis in the Third Sacred War and to pay subsidies to other allies, and the grievance that mattered most to the islands, that the shared money was being diverted, broke out in the open. Institutional resentment had piled up as well. The great business of the league was decided in the Athenian citizen assembly; islanders had neither a vote nor a share in military command, yet they were sent to fight on battlefields chosen in Athens. Add the lobbying of Mausolus of Caria and of the Persian emissaries, and the islands could see a calculable comparison of risks: stay in the league and keep paying for Athens' wars and taxes, or move to the Spartan-led league and keep their autonomy. The timing was equally good. Athens was deep in the Phocidian war and in the northern problem of the Chersonese, its forces scattered across several fronts with gaps left in the defence, and Sparta happened to be waiting in the north, so that almost the whole weight of preparation fell on the Athenian side.
impact: 同盟者戰爭的直接後果，是第二雅典同盟的解體。公元前355年共同庫房的用途被正式廢除，島邦各自加入斯巴達主導的第二赫倫尼克聯盟並取得自治；雅典失去對赫勒斯滂海峽與拜占庭的控制，也失去色雷斯的刻爾索涅斯地峽這塊北方殖民地，隨之而來的是黑海穀物來源的穩定性與關稅收入的下滑。更深的一層影響落在雅典的戰略選擇上。島邦的成功示範讓地中海東岸的城邦看見，離開雅典是可以活命的；而更關鍵的是，雅典為了脫離斯巴達的優勢而向波斯求援，公元前355年簽訂的雅典與波斯條約換來了援軍，也把外族可以自由介入希臘事務這道口子留在國內政治裡，成為日後腓力二世與亞歷山大介入的先例。戰爭留下的技術教訓同樣深：提謨修斯的敗績提醒海軍統帥如何在狹窄海峽佈防，卡布里亞斯的守勢船術與伊菲克拉特斯的裝備改革則成為下一代雅典海軍的改造方向；在內政上，一位名將因遠征而受公眾審訊，即使無罪仍舊鬱卒而亡，成了雅典民主制度中將領與公民大會關係最刺目的註腳。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the Social War was the dissolution of the Second Athenian League. In 355 BC the purposes of the common treasury were formally wound up, the islands entered the Spartan-led Second Hellenic League and obtained autonomy, and Athens lost control of the Hellespont and of Byzantium together with the northern colony of the Thracian Chersonese; with them went the reliability of its Black Sea grain supply and a slice of its revenue. The deeper effect fell on Athenian strategy. The success of the islands showed the cities of the eastern Mediterranean that leaving Athens could be survived, and, more consequentially, Athens, seeking to escape the Spartan advantage, turned to Persia for help: the Athenian-Persian treaty of 355 BC bought troops and left open the door for outside powers to intervene in Greek affairs, a precedent used later by Philip II and Alexander. The technical lessons were equally lasting. The ruin of Timotheus taught naval commanders how to deploy in narrow water, and the defensive seamanship of Chabrias together with the equipment reforms of Iphicrates set the direction in which the next generation of the Athenian navy was rebuilt. In domestic politics, the public trial of a famous general on the strength of a failed expedition, and his death from grief even after acquittal, became the most cutting footnote on the relation between generals and the citizen assembly in Athenian democracy.
result: 結局由島邦聯軍與斯巴達一方取得。聯軍沒有正面攻入雅典，而是切斷海峽與糧道，逼雅典求和；公元前355年雅典與斯巴達議和，島邦獲准自治並加入第二赫倫尼克聯盟，雅典交出刻爾索涅斯與其在愛琴海的一批島嶼據點，第二雅典同盟就此解散，帝國時代告終。戰術層面，聯軍完勝：提謨修斯的分隊在拜占庭外海幾乎被全滅，雅典遠征軍在返航途中不斷被追擊與掠奪，數百艘三列槳船的編制散去大半，國庫與人力都耗到極限。戰略層面，聯軍同樣得手：海峽的門戶打開，黑海小麥線重新落入島邦與斯巴達的勢力範圍，雅典則在隨後的十年裡轉而靠向波斯，反而為日後的馬其頓征服鋪墊了道路。唯一為聯軍保留的隱憂，是他們的勝利並不意味著自由：自治的島邦很快發現新主子斯巴達的聯盟同樣要求它們交出艦隊、提供兵員，而北方的刻爾索涅斯最終落入菲利普二世手中。
resultEn: The victory went to the island coalition together with Sparta. The coalition never marched on Athens; it cut the straits and the grain route until Athens sued for peace. In 355 BC Athens made terms with Sparta, the islands were granted autonomy and entered the Second Hellenic League, Athens handed over the Chersonese and a set of its Aegean island bases, the Second Athenian League was dissolved and the imperial era came to an end. Tactically the result was a clean win for the coalition: Timotheus's squadron was practically wiped out off Byzantium, the Athenian expedition was pursued and plundered all the way home, the order of several hundred triremes dissolved by degrees, and the treasury and the manpower of the city were spent to the limit. Strategically the coalition gained as much: the gate of the straits stood open, the Black Sea grain lane fell once more within the reach of the islands and of Sparta, and Athens, over the following decade, turned to lean on Persia, thereby laying the road for the later conquest of Macedonia. The one shadow left to the victors was that their success bought no freedom: the autonomous islands soon found that their new master, the Spartan league, demanded their fleets and their contingents in turn, and the Chersonese in the north ended up in the hands of Philip II.
